_doc: Feature 0091 §6.5 / D2 — the SCOPE wire contract, as DATA.
READ BY BOTH SIDES, ON PURPOSE. The Python walker WRITES `pruned_dirs`;
the Go backend READS it and turns it into `scanScope`, whose verdict
decides whether a lineage row is `out_of_scope` or eligible for closure.
Neither side owns both halves, and BOTH failure directions are silent:
* report the CONTAINER (a bare `.vscode`) while having read
`.vscode/tasks.json`, and Go's prefix match puts the file that WAS
scanned out of scope. Nothing is mis-closed, so no test notices — but
the scope check returns before the tier rules, so a genuinely repaired
folder-open task stays `open` forever. The one row 0091 exists to
protect becomes the one row it breaks.
* report NOTHING for a directory the walker refused to enter, and Go
judges the row in scope; the deterministic rule then marks a finding
FIXED whose code was never read. That is 0091's reference incident.
Before this file the Python suite pinned the interaction against a
TRANSCRIPTION of the Go predicate (test_0091_editor_config_scope.py), and
the Go suite pinned it against hand-written prefixes. Each half could pass
while the pair was wrong, which is exactly the defect class that shipped in
P1 (a Pydantic model silently dropping the new request field).
The pin is that ONE file is asserted against by TWO suites:
backend/internal/service/scan_scope_contract_test.go   (Go)
agents/shared/tests/contract/test_0091_scan_scope.py    (Python)
Editing this file to make one side pass just moves the failure to the
other language — which is the point.
`pruned_dirs` and `scanned` below were GENERATED by the shipped walker
(shared.tools.file_scanner) over the `tree` described here, not written by
hand. The Go half derives its own expectations from `scanned`: every file
the walker READ must be in scope, and nothing it skipped may be.

tree._doc: A realistic project root: source, two SKIP_DIRS editor directories holding both autorun and unrelated content, a devcontainer (never in SKIP_DIRS), and an ordinary pruned directory.

cases.name: editor_config_on
cases._doc: The shipped default. The walker ENTERS .vscode and .idea to reach the allowlisted autorun files and reports the prune at the granularity actually pruned — the individual files and sub-directories it did not read — never the container it walked into.

cases.name: editor_config_off
cases._doc: VULTURE_SCAN_EDITOR_CONFIG=false, D2's rollback. Nothing in the editor directories is read, so the CONTAINER is the honest prefix again and everything beneath it is correctly out of scope. This case is the control: it proves the case above reports children because the walker entered, not because it stopped reporting containers.
